facts.text: The `tern-plugins/code-puppy` Luau plugin is linked and reported `status: ready` with no problems by `tern plugin list --json`. Its `start`, `interrupt` and `stop` commands, Code Puppy PATH availability, approvals and full GUI rendering are not verified live.

Code Puppy final-response rendering is a two-plugin integration: a generic `render_final_response` hook in Code Puppy core plus `tern-plugins/code-puppy/python-plugin/`, which holds all Tern-specific output. The Luau plugin alone is not sufficient.

The earlier direct TSP design for Code Puppy (`code_puppy/tern_surface.py`, `cli_runner.py`, `rich_renderer.py`, `docs/tern-integration-handoff.md`) is superseded and not part of the current working integration. Its original bytes are preserved in a backup snapshot.

Code Puppy's Tern final-response path has a no-provider live check that rendered `PLUGIN_FLOW_CHECK` through the plugin. Only final non-streamed responses render as native Markdown. Streaming, tools, dialogs and full chat remain Rich/Code Puppy-owned, and a real agent conversation is not live-verified.
`docs/reference/tern-integration-status.md` holds the Tern integration status, including the Code Puppy section that describes the plugin pair and what remains unverified.

A Pi extension alone cannot select the TSP frontend at ordinary `pi` startup. `InteractiveMode.init()` calls `ui.start()` before extensions bind, and `ExtensionAPI` offers no renderer or mode factory, so an extension can only add components inside the already running TUI.

`.pi/lib/tern/run.ts` is an opt-in Pi-in-Tern runner, not a Pi extension. It builds its own session via `createAgentSessionRuntime` and `createAgentSessionFromServices`, and it execs the native `pi` CLI when no TSP hello reply arrives. Ordinary `pi` was not modified.
